scope: Local Wase Download broker/API/converter audit; bounded fixtures and regression tests, not production load testing or a full matrix/penetration test

changes.issue: Graceful SIGTERM cleanup omitted uploads and queued files without active containers
changes.evidenceBeforeFix: Actual local HTTP upload left wase-job-* directory after broker exited
changes.fix: Track every admitted conversion request before asynchronous upload and await its existing cleanup on SIGTERM/SIGINT; reject requests during shutdown

changes.issue: ZIP/TAR repacking accepted Windows drive-absolute and drive-relative paths
changes.evidenceBeforeFix: Both C:\Users\escape.txt and C:escape.txt were successfully repacked in failing security regressions
changes.fix: Reject Windows drive paths as well as POSIX absolute paths, traversal and empty paths

localRuntimeSecurity: per-address queue occupancy returns 429 on third outstanding upload
verification.cleanup: Dedicated test broker stopped; no residual test containers or labeled temporary Docker volumes. Unrelated local matrix workers were not touched.
verification.initialEnvironmentFailure: First smoke attempt used /tmp JOB_ROOT which Colima did not share; all conversions returned 422. Repeated with workspace-shared JOB_ROOT and verified 10 successes. No production configuration was changed.

limitations: Conversion samples cover ten categories, not every declared direction or arbitrary file.
Distributed queue exhaustion and network-level DDoS remain possible; application limits bound resource use but do not guarantee availability.
Broker retains Docker-daemon privileges; worker/host isolation is not a substitute for dedicated infrastructure.
SIGKILL/host crash cleanup still needs administrative stale-artifact handling; this patch covers graceful SIGTERM/SIGINT only.
No Docker/OS CVE scan or exploit-oriented penetration test in this scoped audit.
No production deployment performed by this audit subtask.
